name: browser-app-builder
description: Guide a student from local setup to a planned, tested browser app and GitHub Pages publication, with bundled Campus Designer styling.

interface.shortDescription: Plan, build, evaluate, and publish a browser app. No coding experience is required.
interface.longDescription: Turn a problem you understand into a self-contained browser application, with a saved plan, local revision history, calculation evidence, and GitHub Pages publication. Your agent handles the files and commands; you make the product and model decisions. Five workflow skills select from fourteen approved library skills for charts, diagrams, timelines, schedules, tables, React controls, slides, animation, CSV, data transformation, statistics, and reproducible randomness. Library apps use an agent-managed Node/npm/Vite build; simple apps can still use native browser features without Node. Bundled Campus Designer guidance and library-specific themes provide consistent Duke colors and typography. The live examples include independently reviewed library applications and the earlier version 0.1.1 plain-app trials, all using simulated planning conversations and synthetic data. Local geographic mapping is approved; SQL, optimization and video remain candidates undergoing validation.

io.github.jordanmeyer.label: Pilot candidate · Instructor-built
io.github.jordanmeyer.audience: MBA students building a self-contained decision tool, dashboard, or simulation with an agent.

results.label: Passing browser checks across three library fixtures
Earlier plain-app trials published and verified live
New recipe apps independently reviewed and verified live

io.github.jordanmeyer.method: Version 0.2.0 adds thirteen pinned library recipes exercised through individual browser checks and three synthetic combined fixtures on a configured Mac. Browser suites passed 10 presentation, 13 dashboard and 8 operations checks. Production preview, keyboard interactions, CSV import and narrow layout review exposed and corrected stylesheet, slide-sizing and file-input issues. These are maintainer-authored fixtures, not student outcomes or automatic Work-routing trials. The three linked live applications were built separately with version 0.1.1; their publication and corrected updates remain historical evidence. The ten-recipe campaign now has independently reviewed executive and uploaded-files dashboards plus a seasonal order simulator published through the managed workflow. The 13 executive, 31 uploads and 17 simulator browser checks and live reference calculations passed. Reviews corrected dialog focus, chart descriptions, production-only filter parsing and narrow-screen readability. Simulator review corrected returning-page chart lifecycle and maximum-value chart labels. The process model passed 37 browser checks, independent graph/import/keyboard checks, and live 471.5-to-370.5-minute routing comparisons; review corrected a non-finite assertion gap and long-label readability. The roadmap passed 40 checks and live dependency-delay examples; reviews corrected narrow chart display, invalid-draft messaging and returning-browser state. The same returning-browser check corrected native controls in the uploads and simulator apps. Further campaign apps and specialist recipes remain in progress.
io.github.jordanmeyer.limits: Self-contained apps use bundled public/synthetic data or locally selected files. No backends, logins, external runtime APIs, remote AI, analytics, secret keys or remote fonts/scripts. Managed builds require compatible Node/npm and host file, shell and browser capabilities. Library approval covers the recorded versions/configurations, not arbitrary combinations. Work routing, clean-machine macOS/Windows and novice-student usability remain unverified. Browser checks do not certify a business model or full accessibility.
